source.ref: Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957, Sch. Art. 30(1) (subst. by Act 8 of 2010 w.e.f. 1-4-2010)
source.quoted_text: Sch Art. 30(1) (both columns, official DPAL text) — Lease, on the total amount or value of the average annual rent, premium, fine and money advanced: '(i) term not exceeding one year, residential property — fifty paise for every one hundred rupees [0.5%], subject to a maximum of rupees five hundred; (ii) term not exceeding one year, commercial or industrial property — fifty paise per hundred [0.5%]; (iii) exceeding one year and not exceeding ten years — one rupee per hundred [1%]; (iv) exceeding ten years and not exceeding twenty years — two rupees per hundred [2%]; (v) exceeding twenty years and not exceeding thirty years — three rupees per hundred [3%]; (vi) exceeding thirty years or in perpetuity or does not purport to be for any definite term — the same duty as conveyance under Article 20(1) on the total amount or value of average annual rent, fine, premium and money advanced, OR on the market value of the property, whichever is higher.' Explanation: 'money advanced' includes the security deposit whether refundable or adjustable towards rent.

notes_for_reviewer: CONFIDENCE: HIGH (official DPAL text, both columns). lease_base = avg_annual_rent + premium + fine + money_advanced (money_advanced INCLUDES security deposit, refundable or adjustable, per the Explanation). Term bands in months: ≤12 (≤1yr; residential 0.5% cap Rs 500, commercial/industrial 0.5% no cap) / ≤120 (1%) / ≤240 (2%) / ≤360 (3%) / >360 (conveyance rate on max(lease_base, market_value)). The >30y clause (vi) is in the s.3B 'lease in perpetuity' cess list — cess NOT attached here (most leases aren't perpetuity); attach a conditional cess for the (vi) branch in wave 2. Family-lease proviso (Rs 5,000/3,000/1,000 to wife/husband/father/mother/son/daughter/brother/sister, like gift) NOT yet encoded — questionnaire branch, wave 2.

source.quoted_text: Sch Art. 41 (both columns, official DPAL text): 'Powers of attorney (as defined by section 2(1)(P)) not being a proxy — (a) sole purpose of procuring registration ... single transaction — One hundred rupees; (b) authorising one person or more to act in a single transaction other than (a) — One hundred rupees; (c) authorising not more than five persons to act jointly and severally in more than one transaction or generally — One hundred rupees; (d) authorising more than five but not more than ten persons ... — Two hundred rupees; (e) when given for consideration or when coupled with interest and authorising the attorney to sell any immovable property — the same duty as a Conveyance under Article 20(1) on consideration or market value, whichever is higher; (ea) if relating to construction/development ... by owner/lessee and developer — Two rupees per hundred [2%] on the market value of the undivided share, whichever higher.'

pending_verification.reason: STALE — Karnataka Stamp (Amendment) Act 04 of 2024, assented and in force at once on 03-02-2024, rewrote this Article. Our source PDF (sources/KA/karnataka-stamp-act-1957_dpal-karnataka.pdf) is a stale print whose newest amendment footnote is Act 55 of 2020, so this encoding faithfully followed a text that was already superseded. Founder to re-source from DPAL and encode the new era. Dates before 03-02-2024 remain correct and still compute. Art 41(a)-(c): Rs 100 -> Rs 500; (d): Rs 200 -> Rs 1,000; (f),(g): Rs 50 -> Rs 100; (h): Rs 200 -> Rs 500.

notes_for_reviewer: CONFIDENCE: HIGH for the common cases (a)-(c) = Rs 100 (official DPAL). ESCALATIONS for the questionnaire (NOT this flat rule): (d) 6-10 persons → Rs 200; (e) POA for consideration/coupled-with-interest to sell immovable → Conveyance rate on higher of consideration/market value (the GPA-for-sale pattern); (ea) developer/development POA → 2% of market value of the undivided share (with the Art 5(f) agreement set-off capping it at Rs 200). These forks belong in Flow B.
